notes.general_comments: The November 2021 Listening paper consisted of 37 questions and was the first time the Listening test was multiple-choice for the November session. Candidates overall performed well and most attempted all questions. Candidates should take care when they transfer their answers onto the answer sheet and shade one letter only for Questions 1 to 34, and two letters for Questions 35 to 37 . The French extracts heard by candidates gradually increased in terms of length and complexity and featured simple transactional exchanges, short monologues, conversations, and interviews. The emphasis of the questions moved from assessing the candidates’ ability to identify information contained in short factual pieces to testing their ability to understand specific information, descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, and explanations in longer extracts. The paper differentiated well.
notes.1-8: The extracts were short, straightforward interactions and candidates performed well in this exercise. For Question 4 , some candidates did not know citron and often chose A ( fraise ) instead. For Question 6 , some candidates were not familiar with ventre and selected A ( dents) instead . For Question 7 , some candidates did not identify planche à voile ; C was the most frequent error.
notes.9-14: In this exercise, candidates heard a longer extract which featured an advertisement for a language school in Normandy. Candidates performed well in this exercise. Question 10 was the most demanding and a third of candidates did not identify the correct time, option B . For Question 14 , some candidates did not recognise casquette. There was no clear pattern of incorrect answers.
notes.15-19: This was a matching exercise in which candidates heard a conversation between two friends, Thibault and Olivia, talking about Olivia’s family. Overall candidates performed well in this exercise. Question 15 was attempted well. For Question 16 , nearly two thirds of the candidates selected the correct answer, option A ; the most frequent incorrect answers were B and D . For Question 17 , half the candidates understood raconter des histoires amusantes and me fait rire , successfully selecting F ; a third incorrectly chose option D . Question 18 was the most challenging and under half the candidates chose the correct option D . Many candidates answered Question 19 successfully.
notes.20-28: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview in two parts with Antoine and his uncle Michel about Montréal Comic Arts Festival. The exercise represented a step up in the incline of difficulty of the test. Many candidates answered Question 20 accurately; those who answered incorrectly usually chose distractor A . Question 21 was attempted well. Question 22 was demanding. Over half the cohort identified the time phrases and tenses and successfully selected A , whilst the most frequent incorrect answer was distractor C . Question 23 was answered correctly by many candidates. Those who answered incorrectly heard ce festival québécois and chose distractor C . Many candidates understood ma famille m’offre une BD pour Noël et pour mon anniversaire and selected B in Question 24 . Most candidates chose the correct answer for Question 25 . Over half the cohort answered Question 26 successfully; those who answered incorrectly chose distractor A . Similar numbers of candidates answered Question 27 correctly; there was some uncertainty about numbers ( 40 / 14 ) and distractor B was the most frequent error. Over half the candidates also chose the correct option C in Question 28 . Those who answered this question incorrectly heard passer la soirée and chose distractor A .
notes.29-34: Candidates heard an interview with Benjamin, a French student talking about his work experience. This was an appropriately demanding exercise at this stage of the paper. Under half the candidates understood anxieux and chose the correct answer for Question 29 . Candidates needed to listen carefully to what Benjamin said as distractors A and B referred to his friends, not to him. An equal number of candidates answered Question 30 successfully. Those who answered incorrectly usually chose distractors A and D . Similar numbers of candidates were familiar with envoyer un courriel and chose the correct option D for Question 31 ; incorrect answers were equally split between distractors A and C . Under half the cohort answered Question 32 correctly, with distractor D often being chosen. Similar numbers of candidates answered Question 33 correctly. Candidates needed to listen carefully for mais ce qui me semble essentiel which introduced the main quality, option D . Many candidates answered Question 34 successfully.
notes.35-37: Candidates heard an interview with Mylène who talked about a rally in Africa. For each question in this exercise, candidates had to identify two correct statements from a choice of five. This was an appropriately demanding and challenging exercise at this stage of the paper. For Question 35 , half the cohort correctly chose options A and C ; candidates often chose distractors B and E . They needed to listen carefully to what Mylène said as il y a deux ans applied to her teammate, Anne. Question 36 was the most challenging question in this exercise; a third of candidates correctly chose option B and a few selected option C . Many did not understand that the training involved map reading ( apprendre à trouver mon chemin en utilisant des cartes) and chose distractor D . Many candidates also missed the negative ( on n’avait pas le droit de se servir de nos téléphones ) and selected E . Question 37 was attempted well with over a quarter of the candidates successfully choosing option D and over two thirds selecting option E . Many candidates did not identify the time phrase and future tense ( j’espère qu’à l’avenir on utilisera des voitures électriques ) and chose distractor A . Some candidates were not familiar with une amie d’enfance and selected distractor B .
